text.p: Jeff Gordon became the youngest driver in history to win the Daytona 500, leading his two Hendricks Motorsports teammates to a 1-2-3 finish on Sunday in America's biggest stock car race.

The 25-year-old Gordon, who won the 1995 NASCAR Winston Cup series championship, took the checkered flag under caution ahead of defending series champion Terry Labonte and Ricky Craven, all of whom drive Chevrolets for owner Rick Hendicks, who recently was diagnosed for cancer and did not attend the race.

Gordon used a cellular phone to contact Hendicks as his car was pushed to Victory Lane. "He's the first person I wanted to talk to," said Gordon, who registered his 20th Winston Cup Series victory. "1-2-3. Can you believe this?"
Twice during the 200-lap race around the 2.5-mile Daytona International Speedway course, Gordon had to work his way from the back of the field to regain the lead.

With 33 laps remaining, Gordon was on the verge of being lapped by Bill Elliott, but a caution flag kept him on the lead lap. Later, Gordon fell out of the lead draft, but a dramatic crash involving several of the race leaders moved him into second place.
"I kept on praying 'God, if you want me to glorify you, I'm going to need a caution flag'," Gordon said. With 10 laps remaining, Dale Earnhardt hit the wall along the backstretch.

Earnhardt was hit from behind by defending race champion Dale Jarrett and rolled Earnhardt's car over, and it hit the Ford of Ernie Irvan. Irvan's hood flew into the grandstands, injuring one spectator.

After the restart, Gordon took the lead from Elliott with six laps remaining. A second wreck involving 13 cars took place on lap 197, bringing out the caution flag and ensuring Gordon's triumph. Gordon's winning speed was 148.295 miles per hour.

There were eight caution flags for 29 laps. Labonte never led the race, but was consistently running near the front of the 42-car field the entire race. Craven, who joined the team this season, worked his way up from a 40th-place start.
For Earnhardt, who has won seven Winston Cup Series championships, but has never claimed the Daytona 500 title, the wreck continued his frustrations in the Super Bowl of American Stock Car Racing.

Earnhardt has won 29 other races here at Daytona, but is 0-for-19 in this race. Earnhardt led 48 of the first 49 laps. He somehow put his car back on the track after the race and finished 31st. Mark Martin's Ford dominated most of the race, leading 52 laps, but faded in the final laps.
Rounding out the top 10 were Elliott (Ford); Sterlin Marlin (Chevrolet); Jeremy Mayfield (Ford); Martin (Ford); Ward Burton (Pontiac); Ricky Rudd (Ford) and Darrel Waltrip (Chevrolet).
